subject: Upfront allocation amendment for Growth Plan — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Emma Turner <emma@stratuspay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood Growth Plan — multi-year prepay options

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — StratusPay liked the throughput and observability features. We need to get finance and procurement aligned quickly. Our CFO asked for: a 2–3 year prepay option with a phased consumption (lower usage Y1 that ramps in Y2/Y3), and a clear schedule of term discounts tied to the committed $/month.

Can you send: 1) a pricing grid showing unit economics for 24 vs 36 month prepay at common ramp profiles, 2) suggested ramp breakpoints, and 3) any standard SOW language you require for upfront billing and invoicing cadence?

Target timeline: we hope to present to our procurement committee on 9/20. Is a DocuSign-ready SOW possible by then if we agree on terms?

Appreciate it — Emma

Emma Turner
Director, Strategic Partnerships | StratusPay
emma@stratuspay.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Growth Plan — multi-year prepay options

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Neha (pricing) and Vanessa (finance) to land the mechanics.

High-level proposal (summary, more detail attached):
- Option A: 24-month prepay, 30% of committed annualized allocation billed upfront (then monthly true-ups). Effective discount: 12% off list for the 24-month commitment with a staged ramp: 60% usage Y1 / 100% Y2.
- Option B: 36-month prepay, 20% upfront year-1, effective discount: 18% off list, staged ramp: 40% Y1 / 80% Y2 / 100% Y3.

We attach a pricing_grid_v2.xlsx that models token/unit economics by ramp profile and shows breakpoints where additional discounts trigger (e.g., >$250k ARR equivalent). We can convert the chosen option into SOW language and a DocuSign envelope if you confirm which structure you prefer.

Questions for you: do you need a fixed monthly invoice schedule (same $ each month) or true-ups based on observed consumption? Our finance team prefers upfront allocation + monthly true-up; procurement sometimes asks for fixed invoices for budgeting.

I'll wait for Neha and Vanessa to comment on whether we can push to the 18% for the 36-month or need approval.

— Logan

Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1 (510) 555-0106
[attachment: pricing_grid_v2.xlsx]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing suggestion and approval ask — StratusPay (RDW-4987)

Team — reviewed Logan's initial numbers and StratusPay's ramp ask. My recommended concession package to close on a 24–36 month blended bill: 

Proposal (for internal approval):
- Primary offer: 36-month prepay with a three-step allocation (40% Y1 / 70% Y2 / 100% Y3).
- Discounting: 18% off list for the 36M if signed within two weeks; fallback 13% for 24M if they prefer shorter term.
- SLA/credit: offer a one-time $25k performance credit if we miss the P99 latency SLO in any quarter of Year 1.
- Billing: 25% upfront, balance invoiced quarterly in arrears with monthly usage true-ups. Procurement has asked for a predictable cap; we can include a not-to-exceed that equals 110% of committed allocation.

Conditions and asks:
1) Legal needs to remove auto-renew or add explicit renewal notice.
2) Finance needs to confirm revenue recognition for a 25% upfront structure — Vanessa, can you confirm we can accept this?
3) Sales approval: I can sign off up to 16% discount. Anything >16% requires VP approval (Aditya).

If Aditya signs off on the incremental discount (to 18%) I will prepare a redline of the SOW and the pricing appendix for DocuSign.

Thanks — Neha

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Pricing Strategy | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing suggestion and approval ask — StratusPay (RDW-4987)

All — finance is OK with the 25% upfront / quarterly invoicing cadence provided we: 1) include a PO reference field on the invoice, 2) do not defer recognition beyond standard ARR treatment, and 3) require procurement to provide a signed PO within 30 days of SOW signature.

We can accept the 18% list discount only with documented VP approval (Aditya). I have no objection to the SLA credit structure, but legal must sign off on the exact credit language and the not-to-exceed clause.

Linking the HubSpot deal for context: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/rdw-4987

If Aditya can approve the incremental 2% (from 16% to 18%), I'll instruct billing to generate a DocuSign-ready contract and coordinate the invoice schedule.

— Vanessa

Emma — thanks for the patience. Internal approvals have cleared conditional on a quick VP sign-off to reach the top-tier discount. Summary of the final, DocuSign-ready proposal: 

- Structure: 36-month prepay, allocation schedule 40% (Y1) / 70% (Y2) / 100% (Y3).
- Pricing: 18% off list if signed by 2026-09-27. Otherwise fallback to 13% for 24 months.
- Billing: 25% upfront at signature, then quarterly invoices with monthly true-ups. Invoices will include PO reference field; StratusPay must deliver PO within 30 days of SOW signature.
- SLA credit: one-time $25k credit if P99 latency SLO missed in any quarter of Year 1.

Attachments: StratusPay_SOW_v3.pdf (final draft), pricing_grid_v2.xlsx (model). DocuSign envelope ready: https://www.docusign.com/en/links/rdw-4987-sign

If this looks good, confirm and we will send the DocuSign envelope. If you need the SOW redlined first, tell me which clause and we'll expedite.
